source_text: Age jam, qui voles curiositatem melius exercere in negotio salutis tuae, percurre Ecclesias apostolicas, apud quas ipsae adhuc cathedrae Apostolorum suis locis praesident; apud quas ipsae authenticae litterae eorum recitantur, sonantes vocem et repraesentantes faciem uniuscujusque. Proxima est tibi Achaia? habes Corinthum. Si non longe es a Macedonia, habes Philippos, habes Thessalonicenses. Si potes in Asiam tendere, habes Ephesum. Si autem Italiae adjaces, habes Romam, unde nobis quoque auctoritas praesto est. Ista quam felix Ecclesia! cui totam doctrinam Apostoli cum sanguine suo profuderunt; ubi Petrus passioni Dominicae adaequatur; ubi Paulus Joannis exitu coronatur; ubi Apostolus Joannes, posteaquam, in oleum igneum demersus, nihil passus est, in insulam relegatur; videamus quid didicerit, quid docuerit, cum Africanis quoque Ecclesiis contesserarit. Unum Deum novit, creatorem universitatis, et Christum Jesum ex virgine Maria Filium Dei creatoris, et carnis resurrectionem; Legem et Prophetas cum evangelicis et apostolicis litteris miscet, et inde potat fidem; eam aqua signat, Sancto Spiritu vestit, eucharistia pascit, ad martyrium exhortatur, et ita adversus hanc institutionem neminem recipit. Haec est institutio, non dico jam quae futuras haereses praenuntiabat, sed de qua haereses prodierunt. Sed non fuerunt ex illa, ex quo factae sunt adversus illam. Etiam de olivae nucleo mitis et optimae et necessariae asper oleaster oritur; etiam de papavere ficus gratissimae et suavissimae ventosa et vana caprificus exsurgit. Ita et haereses de nostro frutice, non nostro genere; veritatis grano, sed mendacio sylvestres.
pass_a_gloss: Now, if you want to exercise your curiosity better in the matter of your salvation, run through the apostolic Churches, in which the very chairs of the Apostles still preside in their own places; in which their authentic letters are read, sounding the voice and representing the face of each one. If Achaia is near you, you have Corinth. If you are not far from Macedonia, you have Philippi, you have the Thessalonians. If you can stretch into Asia, you have Ephesus. If, however, you are adjacent to Italy, you have Rome, from which also authority is at hand for us. What a happy Church this is! To which the Apostles poured out all their doctrine with their own blood; where Peter is equal to the Lord's passion; where Paul is crowned with John's exit; where the Apostle John, after he was immersed in burning oil and suffered nothing, is relegated to an island; let us see what he learned, what he taught, when he was a fellow-contestant with the African Churches. He knows one God, the creator of the universe, and Christ Jesus, the Son of God the creator, from the virgin Mary, and the resurrection of the flesh; he mixes the Law and the Prophets with the evangelical and apostolic letters, and from there he drinks faith; he seals it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, exhorts it to martyrdom, and thus he receives no one against this institution. This is the institution, I do not say now which predicted future heresies, but from which heresies have come forth. But they were not from it, since they were made against it. Also from the nucleus of the olive, a wild and useless oleaster arises; also from the poppy, a windy and vain caprificus rises from the most pleasing and sweetest fig. So also heresies arise from our fruit, not our kind; from the grain of truth, but from the forest of lies.
pass_b_english: If you want to pursue your curiosity more profitably for the sake of your salvation, visit the apostolic Churches where the very chairs of the Apostles still preside in their own places, where their authentic letters are read aloud, sounding the voice and representing the face of each one. If Achaia lies near you, you have Corinth; if you are not far from Macedonia, you have Philippi and the Thessalonians; if you can reach Asia, you have Ephesus; if you border Italy, you have Rome, from which authority is also at hand for us.

What a fortunate Church this is! The Apostles poured out their whole teaching upon it with their own blood; here Peter matches the Lord's passion, here Paul is crowned with John's end; here the Apostle John, after being plunged into boiling oil and suffering nothing, was banished to an island. Let us see what he learned and taught when he stood alongside the African Churches. He knows one God, the Creator of the universe, and Christ Jesus, the Son of God the Creator, born of the virgin Mary, and the resurrection of the flesh; he blends the Law and the Prophets with the evangelical and apostolic writings, and from them he draws faith; he seals it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, urges it toward martyrdom, and so admits no one against this rule.

This is the rule — I do not say merely the one that foretold future heresies, but the one from which heresies have arisen. Yet they did not spring from it, because they were formed against it. Even from the olive's kernel a wild, useless oleaster grows; even from the poppy a windy, empty caprifig springs from the most pleasing and sweetest fig. So heresies spring from our fruit, not our kind; from the grain of truth, but as a forest of lies.
